5 Ways People Can Tell AI Wrote Your Post

You wrote the post. Or you asked an AI to write it and then hit publish. Either way, people scroll past it and you don't know why.

Most of the time it's the same few habits. Readers have seen thousands of AI posts by now, and they spot them in a second. Here are five of the common ones.

Free: The Robot Tells

12 tells that scream 'AI wrote this', each with a 30-second fix.

Send Me The Checklist

1. The question opener

"Ever wondered why your posts get no sales?" Nobody talks like that. Start with the point instead. Say what you saw or what you did.

2. Everything comes in threes

Fast, simple, effective. Clear, concise, compelling. AI loves lists of three. Real people say one thing and move on. Pick the best word and cut the other two.

3. Big empty words

"Unlock your potential." "Elevate your business." "Game-changer." These words sound important and say nothing. Swap each one for the thing that actually happens. What does the reader get? What do they do on Monday?

4. A tidy bow at the end

"At the end of the day, success is a journey." Stop one line early. End on your last real point or a plain question.

5. No you in it

A post with no story, no name, no mess is easy to spot. Add one real detail only you would know. A number from your week. A mistake you made. A customer question.

  • Read it out loud. If you would never say it to a friend, change it.
  • Cut the first sentence. Most posts start better on the second one.
  • Add one detail from your own life.

That's five. There are more, and each one has a 30-second fix. I put them all in one checklist with before and after rewrites so you can fix a post in a couple of minutes.
